title: A dose-ranging randomized, open-label study evaluating the effect of bilateral intravitreal injection of GS010 at two dose levels on visual acuity and retinal mitochondrial activity in patients affected with ND4 Leber Hereditary Optic Neuropathy – The REVISE Study
official: A dose-ranging randomized, open-label study evaluating the effect of bilateral intravitreal injection of GS010 at two dose levels on visual acuity and retinal mitochondrial activity in patients affected with ND4 Leber Hereditary Optic Neuropathy – The REVISE Study
summary: Main objective: To assess the efficacy of bilateral GS010 IVT administered in patients with ND4-LHON, by determining the BCVA change from baseline to 1.5 years post-treatment in the study eyes at two different doses.
conditions:
Leber Hereditary Optic Neuropathy due to mutations in the mitochondrial
NADH Dehydrogenase 4 gene
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Aged 15 years or older at the time of vision loss onset
2. Willing and able to comply with the protocol, follow study instructions, attend study visits as required and complete all study assessments
3. Patient – and parent/legal guardian if the patient is under 18 years of age – has provided signed, written informed consent
4. Clinically manifested vision loss due to ND4 LHON in both eyes
5. BCVA of at least LogMAR +2.39, measured at the FrACT scale, in both eyes
6. Documented results of genotyping showing the presence of pathogenic LHON-associated mutation(s) in the ND4 mitochondrial gene and the absence of other pathogenic LHON-associated mutations in the patient’s mitochondrial DNA; absence of pathogenic mutations, other than the ND4 LHON-causing mutation(s), which are known to cause pathology of the optic nerve, retina or afferent visual system. Historic results of genetic analysis are acceptable upon Sponsor approval.
7. Vision loss duration from 6 months to 1.5 years in the first affected eye at the Inclusion visit (Day -1)
8. No limitations to OCT image collection that would prevent high quality, reliable images from being obtained in both eyes, as determined by the reading center
9. Clear ocular media and adequate pupillary dilation to permit thorough ocular examination, as assessed by the Investigator
10. Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) negative serology
11. Female patients of childbearing potential must agree to use effective methods of birth control for up to 6 months after Treatment visit (Day 0). Male patients must agree to use condoms with their female partners for up to 6 months after Treatment visit (Day 0).
Exclusion criteria:
1. Any known allergy or hypersensitivity to GS010 or any of its constituents
2. Use of any investigational drug, or device, within 90 days, or 5 half-lives, preceding the Inclusion visit (Day-1), whichever is longer, or plans to participate in another study of an investigational drug or device during the study period
3. Previous treatment with ocular gene therapy in either eye.
4. Pregnancy or breast-feeding
5. Contraindication to IVT in any eye according to the Investigator’s clinical judgment and international guidelines (Avery, 2014)
6. Prior intraocular surgery or procedure or IVT, which occurred 6 months prior to inclusion and is considered of clinical relevance per Investigator assessment, or planned intraocular surgery or procedure
7. Presence of optic neuropathy from any cause except LHON, as determined by the Investigator
8. History of recurrent uveitis (idiopathic or immune-related) or active intraocular inflammation, as determined by the Investigator
9. Indication of a unilateral treatment with GS010, as determined by the Investigator: • Unilateral or asymmetric ND4 LHON disease: only one eye affected with a vision loss due to ND4 LHON, and the fellow eye with preserved BCVA (LogMAR 0 or close to 0); • Amblyopia: unilateral treatment of the functional eye with a vision loss due to ND4 LHON; • Patient’s desire for unilateral treatment
10. Ingestion of idebenone less than 7 days prior to the Inclusion visit (Day -1)
11. Inability to tolerate the anti-inflammatory regimen
12. Presence of ocular disease (excluding LHON), or systemic disease, or condition (including medications and laboratory test abnormalities) that could compromise patient safety or interfere with assessment of efficacy and safety, as determined by the Investigator
